key_insight: Fermion-to-qubit encodings such as BK and XBK can be interpreted as geometric objects, where hypergraph connectivity and coupling-space transport reveal structure beyond simple Hamiltonian translation.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum-simulation engineers new diagnostics for choosing and analyzing encodings, potentially improving how many-body models are represented, compared, and organized on qubit hardware.
method: Built weighted hypergraph representations for BK-encoded Hamiltonians.
Defined a geometric observable comparing kinetic vs interaction connectivity and derived its exact dependence on interaction strength.
Used XBK coupling-space probability measures and optimal transport to track interaction-driven reorganization.
evidence_signal: The framework was tested on the Hubbard, spinless tV, single impurity Anderson, and Kitaev models, showing consistent geometric signatures across distinct many-body systems.
watch_item: The results are encoding-specific and rely on exact analytical structure, so extending the approach to noisy, approximate, or hardware-constrained encodings may require additional validation.
paper_title: A Geometric Theory of Fermion-to-Qubit Encodings
